newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends steady-up, late sales on estimate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends steady-up, late sales on estimate.

text.p: Corn futures on the CBOT ended flat to slightly higher, but gains were trimmed late by ideas that a private crop estimate expected to be released Friday will be bearish for the market, traders said.
"Sparks is expected to come out with a bearish corn crop estimate tomorrow," said one trader.
The USDA will release its final crop production estimate on Jan. 10, and many expect the private consulting firm Sparks Cos. of Memphis, Tenn. to raise its corn estimate.
At a meeting in Kansas City in December, the CEO of Sparks forecast the final corn crop between 9.3 billion and 9.4 billion bushels.
Commercial buying provided futures with the strength to rally in earlier trade. Cargill bought six million bushels of March, which brought its total since Monday to nearly 40 million bushels.
Ideas that it is getting too dry in Argentina also helped keep corn futures firm throughout the session, traders said.
